what_it_does: When chip designers create a library of standard logic cells — the tiny building blocks like AND gates and flip-flops that make up a digital chip — each cell must be carefully characterized to know how fast it switches and how much power it draws across many combinations of voltage, temperature, and manufacturing process variation (called PVT corners). Traditionally this is done by running a physics-level circuit simulator (SPICE) for every cell under every corner, which becomes extremely expensive as the number of corners grows into the hundreds. This paper proposes replacing most of those simulations with a generative AI model that learns the patterns in the timing data and can synthesize realistic timing values for corners it was never explicitly simulated on, dramatically cutting simulation cost without sacrificing accuracy.
